text: The Marisol Trench probe reached 9,400 metres during a trial descent off the coast of Caldera Point, according to the coastal science office. The uncrewed vessel, launched Tuesday from the survey ship Pelican Star, transmitted temperature, pressure and seismic readings before operators ended the dive at 4:18 p.m. due to stable conditions, officials said. The mark is the deepest penetration yet for the region’s marine survey program and exceeds last year’s benchmark by 600 metres. “This gives us a clearer picture of the trench floor than we’ve ever had before,” said Mira Solen, head of the Harbour Regional Marine Authority. Engineers will now analyze the data for signs of underwater fault activity and unusual thermal vents.
